title: Advanced Paste: Paste with AI can't find Foundry Local models
author: jacktose
summary: Foundry Local 0.10.3 is healthy and has loaded and cached models, but Advanced Paste uses the legacy 0.3.0 SDK path and presents an empty model list.

status.label: Design ready for approval
status.detail: The new public comment identifies a Foundry API rearchitecture; the implementation design updates discovery and preserves errors instead of reporting a false empty cache.

next_action.label: Approve Foundry Local SDK migration design
next_action.reason: The report, follow-up confirmation, public Foundry API change, and repository code identify a concrete compatibility fix.

judgment.rationale: The issue supplies a complete reproduction against Foundry Local 0.10.3, including a healthy service, loaded and cached models, successful CLI use, and a persistent empty state in Advanced Paste. The latest comment links to a public commit describing a complete Foundry API change, which reinforces the repository evidence that PowerToys still calls the legacy SDK contract.
evidence: The report shows Foundry Local 0.10.3 Ready, phi-4-mini loaded, two cached models, and successful CLI chat while PowerToys reports no downloaded models.
The reporter tried refresh, server restart, PowerToys restart, and another model without changing the empty state.
The issue's attached archive was rejected by the automated triage comment; its contents are not treated as verified log evidence.
The latest public comment links to https://github.com/microsoft/foundry-local/commit/255cb454ea69331adf6fbd423aba2da8e9075f52 and states that the Foundry API changed completely.
FoundryClient.ListCatalogModels catches listing failures and returns its cached list, while ListCachedModels returns an empty list on failure.
FoundryLocalModelProvider.GetModelsAsync maps an empty cached result directly to the Settings no-model state.
Related open issue #50368 independently reports an empty Service URL and invalid-URI failures with Foundry Local 0.10.3; it is corroborating evidence, not a confirmed duplicate link.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the SDK migration and typed discovery-error design, then validate the selected package and API overloads against the supported target framework.

fix_assessment.rationale: No PowerToys pull request or other concrete fix covers the Foundry Local 0.10.x discovery incompatibility. The newer public API-change report strengthens the case for replacing the legacy integration rather than adding another retry.

proposed_fixes.title: Migrate Advanced Paste to the current Foundry Local SDK and preserve discovery failures
proposed_fixes.root_cause: PowerToys pins the CLI-dependent Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local 0.3.0 SDK. Foundry Local 0.10.3 uses a reworked SDK and daemon contract, so legacy endpoint and model-list calls can fail while the CLI remains healthy. FoundryClient then converts those failures into an empty collection, which the UI renders as no downloaded models.
plan: Select and pin the supported Windows Foundry Local SDK package/version for the repository target framework.
Replace the legacy FoundryLocalManager endpoint and listing calls with the current manager, catalog, cached-model, loaded-model, and model-chat-client lifecycle behind the FoundryClient boundary.
Return a typed discovery failure from the provider boundary and distinguish it from a successful empty cached-model result in Advanced Paste Settings.
Add deterministic fake-provider coverage for successful discovery, empty discovery, initialization failure, and listing failure, then run targeted builds and tests.
verification: With Foundry Local 0.10.3 Ready and phi-4-mini loaded, refresh the Advanced Paste provider dialog and verify that the model is selectable.
When discovery fails, verify Settings shows an actionable discovery-error state rather than the no-model message.
With a successful empty cache, verify the existing no-model guidance remains unchanged.
Load the selected model and run Paste with AI through the same local provider to verify discovery and inference use the same model identity.

confidence.rationale: The package pin, current source control flow, complete public reproduction, independent 0.10.3 report, and the linked public API-change commit all converge on the same compatibility boundary. Exact package names and overloads still require compile-time confirmation, but that does not change the identified failing layer.

issue_context.summary: Advanced Paste cannot enumerate Foundry Local 0.10.3 models even though the Foundry service and CLI can load and use them.
known_information: The reporter installed Foundry Local 0.10.3 and loaded phi-4-mini.
Foundry status reported Ready, a reachable localhost service, one loaded model, and two cached models.
The Foundry CLI chat command worked, while Advanced Paste displayed no downloaded models.
Refreshes, service restart, PowerToys restart, and loading another model did not resolve the issue.
A second public commenter confirmed the same experience.
The latest commenter linked a public Foundry Local commit and said the API changed completely.
PowerToys source pins Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local 0.3.0 and contains the legacy manager/listing calls described in the design.
There is no assignee, linked PowerToys fix, or maintainer-confirmed duplicate in the live issue.
inferences: The 0.3.0 SDK contract is likely incompatible with the Foundry Local 0.10.3 architecture.
The false empty state is likely caused by FoundryClient swallowing discovery exceptions.
Issue #50368 appears to be a closely related 0.10.3 report, but no upstream duplicate relationship has been established.
issue_context.analysis: The report already contains the decisive service-health and model-state evidence, so another generic log request would not improve triage. The repository code confirms both a legacy integration boundary and an error-to-empty conversion. The current action should therefore be a concrete SDK migration and error-state design, with package/API compatibility left as an implementation verification item.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body, all three comments, labels, assignees, activity, attachments, and linked-work signals.
Inspected Directory.Packages.props, LanguageModelProvider.csproj, FoundryClient, FoundryLocalModelProvider, FoundryLocalPasteProvider, AdvancedPastePage, and the custom-action provider path.
Confirmed that FoundryClient.ListCatalogModels and ListCachedModels suppress failures and that the Settings path treats an empty result as no downloaded models.
Reviewed the public Foundry Local API-change commit linked by the latest commenter.
Searched related Foundry Local issues, including #45340 and open issue #50368; #45340 covers the older 0.8.119 fixed-port behavior and is not the same 0.10.x contract failure.
No upstream PowerToys PR or issue-linked implementation currently covers this report.

information_gaps.information: The exact supported current Windows package/version and overload signatures for the repository target framework
information_gaps.why_needed: The migration must compile, package the correct native assets, and define the minimum supported Foundry Local version.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm during implementation with package restore, API metadata, and targeted x64 builds.

information_gaps.information: Whether the migrated provider should use the SDK-native chat client or its OpenAI-compatible web endpoint
information_gaps.why_needed: The choice affects model loading, endpoint lifetime, and inference compatibility after discovery is fixed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Validate both supported paths against Foundry Local 0.10.3 during targeted integration testing.

design.root_cause: The current integration constructs Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local 0.3.0's legacy FoundryLocalManager, reads its Endpoint/ServiceUri, and calls legacy catalog, cached-model, and loaded-model methods. Foundry Local 0.10.3 replaced that service-based architecture. When the legacy calls fail, FoundryClient catches the exceptions and returns empty data; FoundryLocalModelProvider then maps that empty data to the Settings no-model message.
evidence: [Observed] The issue reports Foundry Local 0.10.3 Ready with a loaded phi-4-mini, two cached models, and successful CLI chat.
[Observed] The latest public comment links to a Foundry Local commit and states that the API changed completely.
[Observed] FoundryClient uses new FoundryLocalManager(), Endpoint, ServiceUri, ListCatalogModelsAsync, ListCachedModelsAsync, ListLoadedModelsAsync, and LoadModelAsync.
[Observed] FoundryClient.ListCatalogModels and ListCachedModels swallow exceptions and return empty/cached collections.
[Observed] FoundryLocalModelProvider.GetModelsAsync emits ModelDetails from the cached collection without an error state.
[Inferred] The legacy SDK calls are incompatible with 0.10.3 and the swallowed errors create the false empty UI.

affected_files.purpose: Central package version pinning for the Foundry Local integration.
References the Foundry Local SDK used by the common provider.
Owns Foundry SDK construction, service readiness, model discovery, and loading.
Maps Foundry models to the Advanced Paste model contract and creates an inference client.
Runs custom actions through the discovered Foundry model and translates provider failures.
Displays Foundry Local availability, model discovery, and empty/error states.
Provides localized user-facing Foundry discovery and failure text.
Hosts deterministic provider and custom-action regression coverage.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The common provider is compiled against the legacy 0.3.0 Foundry Local SDK.
implementation_steps.change: Pin the current Windows-compatible package/version selected from the supported Foundry Local 0.10.x API and update the project reference only if the package identity changes. Record the minimum supported Foundry Local version in the relevant provider documentation or user-facing error guidance.
edge_cases: Confirm x64 and ARM64 native assets and the existing target framework.
Do not retain legacy constructors or endpoint properties solely because they compile against a compatibility package.
Keep the package choice explicit if the current API is split into a base and Windows-specific package.
tests: Restore and build LanguageModelProvider for the supported Windows architectures.
Inspect the resolved package API metadata before changing the adapter.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The client creates a legacy manager, reads legacy endpoint state, calls legacy listing/loading methods, and turns all discovery exceptions into empty or false results.
implementation_steps.change: Introduce a small adapter around the selected current SDK manager/catalog/model interfaces. Initialize through the current async contract, retrieve catalog/cached/loaded models from the current catalog API, map stable model IDs and aliases, honor cancellation, and propagate a typed discovery exception instead of returning a false empty success.
edge_cases: Preserve the existing PATH refresh retry only if the selected SDK still depends on installed command discovery.
Do not hide cancellation or convert a service/API failure into an empty successful result.
Respect singleton or manager lifetime requirements of the current SDK.
Keep model IDs stable enough for existing fl:// settings migration.
tests: Fake the adapter for successful catalog discovery, successful empty cache, initialization failure, and listing failure.
Verify cancellation propagates from the provider call.
Verify a failed listing is distinguishable from an empty successful listing.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The provider maps legacy cached DTOs, loads through the legacy client, and creates an OpenAI-compatible client from a legacy service URI.
implementation_steps.change: Consume the new adapter result, preserve aliases and model IDs, use the current SDK model load/chat-client path where supported, and retain the OpenAI-compatible endpoint only when it is the documented supported inference surface. Preserve typed discovery and load errors for the caller.
edge_cases: Do not create a client for a model absent from the current catalog unless the SDK explicitly supports that state.
Keep refresh/retry behavior bounded and cancellation-aware.
Preserve existing fl:// model references or provide a one-time migration for changed IDs.
Do not report provider availability as true when discovery initialization failed.
tests: Verify current model metadata maps to ModelDetails and preserves aliases.
Verify loaded and unloaded model paths use the selected SDK lifecycle.
Verify discovery and load exceptions reach the custom-action error boundary.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: An empty result from either a real empty cache or a swallowed SDK exception displays the no-downloaded-model message.
implementation_steps.change: Handle typed discovery failures separately, log them with the provider context, show localized actionable error text, and reserve no-model guidance for a confirmed successful empty cache.
edge_cases: Marshal all visual-state changes through the existing UI dispatcher.
Keep Save disabled until a valid model is selected.
Do not expose raw endpoint data or sensitive exception contents in localized UI.
Preserve the existing unavailable state when Foundry Local is not installed or cannot start.
tests: A discovery exception shows the discovery-error state.
A successful empty cache shows the existing no-model state.
A non-empty cache enables model selection and Save.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The current test surface does not prove behavior across the 0.3.0-to-0.10.x discovery boundary.
implementation_steps.change: Add fake-adapter tests for the discovery state machine and a regression test that a discovered 0.10.3 model can execute a custom action without falling back to the empty state.
edge_cases: Cover both loaded and cached-but-not-loaded models.
Validate that cancellation remains distinct from provider failure.
tests: Run the focused AdvancedPaste unit-test selector and the LanguageModelProvider build.
Run the affected Settings UI tests when the test project is available.

verify: Install Foundry Local 0.10.3, download and load phi-4-mini, and confirm the CLI reports Ready and a loaded model.
Open Advanced Paste provider settings before the change and capture the false empty state as the baseline.
Install the fixed build, refresh the provider, and verify phi-4-mini appears and can be selected.
Save the model and run a small Paste with AI custom action.
Inject or simulate a discovery exception and verify the UI reports discovery failure rather than no models.
Run the existing targeted LanguageModelProvider and AdvancedPaste tests and supported Windows builds.
risks: SDK migration can change native assets, initialization lifetime, model IDs, and inference APIs; contain this behind the FoundryClient adapter.
Older Foundry Local installations may no longer be supported; document the minimum version and provide a clear unavailable message.
The SDK-native chat client and OpenAI-compatible endpoint may have different streaming, cancellation, and model-load semantics; validate the chosen path with 0.10.3.
Changing error propagation can affect Settings and custom-action callers; add explicit empty-versus-failure tests before removing the legacy catches.
alternatives: A UI-only wording change would leave model discovery and inference broken.
Adding more retries to the legacy manager would not address the public 0.10.x API rearchitecture.
A direct REST fallback was not selected because the current supported endpoint and model lifecycle must first be established from the new SDK contract.
Treating #50368 as a duplicate without maintainer confirmation was avoided; it is recorded as corroborating related work.

actions.label: Approve Foundry Local SDK migration design

comment.body: Approve the implementation-grade Foundry Local SDK migration and discovery-error design for Issue 50152. This artifact records the proposed PowerToys changes; no upstream comment or repository write is made by approval alone.

actions.note: Design approval is a maintainer workflow control; it does not post to the upstream issue.
